note: MULTI-DISPLAY HOMING CONTRACT (Phase B3 documentation-as-fixture). Two displays D1 {0,0,1440,900} + D2 {1440,0,1440,900}; an empty tree; TWO tileable newcomers whose observed frames BOTH physically land on D1 (w1 [100,100,800,600], w2 [300,300,800,600]). G::assign_display homes each by MAX frame/usable overlap, so both home to D1's mount — and ensure_scaffold only creates a mount per OCCUPIED display, so D2 (empty) gets NO mount. Final: root → [d:1 → i:w:2[w:1,w:2]]; d:2 ABSENT. This PINS the homing policy: a new window homes GEOMETRICALLY (to the display its frame overlaps most), NOT by an empty-display-preference. The operator's 'fill BOTH screens' would require a DIFFERENT policy (prefer an empty display when one exists) — surfaced as an open decision in the Phase-B report, NOT changed here. The cross-display populate-both case (windows whose frames DO land on separate displays each get their own mount) is sync-bootstrap-multi-display.
